title: The admirable friend
hookLine: Ananda says good friendship is half the holy life; the Buddha says it is the whole (SN 45.2)

lines: HOW MUCH RESTS ON GOOD FRIENDS?
cards: Half. That was Ananda's number. Tradition remembers him as the Buddha's cousin and, for many years, his attendant: the one who carried the bowl and remembered the talks.
One day he came to the Buddha with something he had worked out about the spiritual life: how much of it rests on good friends. Half, he said. Good friendship is half of the holy life.
It sounds like a generous answer. The Buddha didn't accept it.

teach.b: The scene is in a short discourse in the Samyutta Nikaya.
Ananda says, in paraphrase: good friendship, good companionship, good comradeship, this is half of the holy life. And the Buddha answers: not so, Ananda. It is the whole of the holy life.
Someone with admirable friends, he says, can be expected to develop and cultivate the noble eightfold path.
Then he points to himself: it's by relying on him as an admirable friend that beings are freed from birth, aging and death. The Pali is kalyanamitta. Kalyana means good, beautiful, lovely.
Mitta means friend, from the same family as metta, loving-kindness, the first word of this path. So an admirable friend isn't just a pleasant one. It's someone whose goodness rubs off on you.

teach.h: THE FIRST THING THAT RIPENS THE MIND.
teach.b: Elsewhere the Buddha says that when the mind isn't yet ripe, the very first thing that helps it ripen is an admirable friend.

And in a long talk to a young householder, he describes the real friend: one who helps you when you're careless, who's the same in good times and bad, who points you toward what's good, and who is glad when you do well.
So in this teaching, friendship isn't a nice extra beside the practice, something for weekends. It's the ground. Who you spend time with shapes what you think, what you laugh at, what you let slide.
And it runs both ways: you can be that friend for someone.

how: Buddhists across traditions treat the admirable friend, a teacher or a fellow practitioner, as central to practice, and many describe choosing good companions as part of the path itself.

o: a friend whose goodness helps you grow
a lifelong friend from your own family
a teacher you must obey without question

games.q: match the pieces of the admirable friend.

s: the Buddha agreed that friendship is half of the holy life
he said: not so, Ananda. it is the whole of the holy life.
mitta, friend, is related to metta, loving-kindness
the Buddha called himself an admirable friend
he said relying on him as an admirable friend frees beings from birth, aging and death.

games.q: you're Ananda. you've just told the Buddha that good friendship is half of the holy life. what does he say?
o: not so: it's the whole of the holy life.
games.why: not so, Ananda. it is the whole of the holy life. someone with admirable friends can be expected to develop and cultivate the eightfold path.

practice: Name one admirable friend, someone whose goodness has rubbed off on you, alive or not, near or far; picture their face, remember one moment when they pointed you toward something good, and silently thank them.
Then think of one person for whom you might be that friend. Let them both rest in your mind, and then rest in the breath.

wordCard.voice: Kalyanamitta. The admirable friend, whose goodness rubs off on you. Not half the holy life, the Buddha says: the whole of it.

carryVoice: Your line: the whole of the path. Not half, the Buddha said: all of it. Rest well, friend.

sources.ref: Samyutta Nikaya 45.2, Upaddha Sutta (half the holy life)
Anguttara Nikaya 9.1 / Udana 4.1, Meghiya (the first condition)
Digha Nikaya 31, Sigalovada Sutta (the true friend)
